"""A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph.

Design notes (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * The graph is kept as a single dict ``_deps`` mapping
        task name -> set(names of that task's DIRECT dependencies).
    Registering a task with no dependencies stores an empty set.
  * "task depends_on dep" means ``dep`` must run BEFORE ``task``; it is
    recorded by adding ``dep`` to ``_deps[task]``.
  * Everything is deterministic: there is no randomness, wall-clock, or
    network use anywhere, and any ordering exposed to callers is sorted.
  * ``topo_order()`` runs Kahn's algorithm with an alphabetically sorted
    frontier: whenever several tasks are simultaneously free (all of their
    dependencies already placed) it emits them in alphabetical order.

Public API (do not rename without updating callers):
  add_task(name), add_dependency(task, depends_on),
  tasks(), dependencies(name), topo_order()
"""


class Scheduler:
    def __init__(self):
        # name -> set of direct dependency names
        self._deps = {}

    # ----- graph construction --------------------------------------------
    def add_task(self, name):
        """Register a task. Idempotent: re-adding an existing task is a no-op
        and never clears its recorded dependencies."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            self._deps[name] = set()

    def add_dependency(self, task, depends_on):
        """Record that ``task`` depends on ``depends_on`` (so ``depends_on``
        must run first). Both tasks are auto-registered if new."""
        self.add_task(task)
        self.add_task(depends_on)
        self._deps[task].add(depends_on)

    # ----- graph reads ----------------------------------------------------
    def tasks(self):
        """Sorted list of all registered task names."""
        return sorted(self._deps.keys())

    def dependencies(self, name):
        """Sorted list of ``name``'s DIRECT dependencies."""
        return sorted(self._deps[name])

"""A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph.

Design notes (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * The graph is kept as a single dict ``_deps`` mapping
        task name -> set(names of that task's DIRECT dependencies).
    Registering a task with no dependencies stores an empty set.
  * "task depends_on dep" means ``dep`` must run BEFORE ``task``; it is
    recorded by adding ``dep`` to ``_deps[task]``.
  * Everything is deterministic: there is no randomness, wall-clock, or
    network use anywhere, and any ordering exposed to callers is sorted.
  * ``topo_order()`` runs Kahn's algorithm with an alphabetically sorted
    frontier: whenever several tasks are simultaneously free (all of their
    dependencies already placed) it emits them in alphabetical order.

Public API (do not rename without updating callers):
  add_task(name), add_dependency(task, depends_on),
  tasks(), dependencies(name), topo_order()
"""


class Scheduler:
    def __init__(self):
        # name -> set of direct dependency names
        self._deps = {}

    # ----- graph construction --------------------------------------------
    def add_task(self, name):
        """Register a task. Idempotent: re-adding an existing task is a no-op
        and never clears its recorded dependencies."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            self._deps[name] = set()

    def add_dependency(self, task, depends_on):
        """Record that ``task`` depends on ``depends_on`` (so ``depends_on``
        must run first). Both tasks are auto-registered if new."""
        self.add_task(task)
        self.add_task(depends_on)
        self._deps[task].add(depends_on)

    # ----- graph reads ----------------------------------------------------
    def tasks(self):
        """Sorted list of all registered task names."""
        return sorted(self._deps.keys())

    def dependencies(self, name):
        """Sorted list of ``name``'s DIRECT dependencies."""
        return sorted(self._deps[name])

    # ----- ordering -------------------------------------------------------
    def topo_order(self):
        """Return EVERY registered task in dependency order: each task appears
        after all of its (transitive) dependencies.

        Deterministic: Kahn's algorithm with an alphabetically sorted
        frontier. While tasks remain, the next emitted task is the
        alphabetically smallest one whose (still-unplaced) dependencies have
        all already been placed.

        Raises ValueError if the graph contains a cycle, because then no order
        can place every task after all of its dependencies.
        """
        # Work on a copy of the adjacency; the stored graph is never mutated.
        remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        order = []
        while remaining:
            # Tasks all of whose remaining dependencies are already placed;
            # sorted so the alphabetically smallest is emitted first.
            frontier = sorted(
                name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps
            )
            if not frontier:  # a cycle: every remaining task still waits
                break
            name = frontier[0]
            del remaining[name]
            order.append(name)
            # Placing ``name`` satisfies one dependency of each dependent.
            for deps in remaining.values():
                deps.discard(name)
        if remaining:
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no topological order exists for "
                "tasks %r" % (sorted(remaining),)
            )
        return order

# taskdag

A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph, used as a teaching
toy.

Current capabilities:
  * register tasks and dependency edges (`add_task` / `add_dependency`)
  * read the graph back (`tasks` / `dependencies`)
  * order the whole graph (`topo_order`) — Kahn's algorithm with an
    alphabetically sorted frontier, so the result is deterministic

See `taskdag/scheduler.py` for the design notes. Keep the adjacency design
(`name -> set of direct dependency names`); new features should build on
`_deps` rather than replacing it.

"""Smoke tests that ship with the seed. These exercise only the seed feature
set (graph construction and reads). Keep them green."""
from taskdag.scheduler import Scheduler


def test_add_and_list():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("a")
    s.add_task("b")
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b"]
    assert s.dependencies("b") == ["a"]


def test_add_dependency_autoregisters():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("y", "x")
    assert s.tasks() == ["x", "y"]
    assert s.dependencies("y") == ["x"]
    assert s.dependencies("x") == []


def test_add_task_idempotent():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_task("b")  # must not wipe b's dependency on a
    assert s.dependencies("b") == ["a"]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_add_and_list()
    test_add_dependency_autoregisters()
    test_add_task_idempotent()

"""Tests for cycle safety.

The scheduler must refuse to build cycles:
  * add_dependency(x, x) raises ValueError;
  * add_dependency(task, depends_on) raises ValueError -- leaving the graph
    unchanged -- when depends_on already reaches task through existing edges;
  * has_cycle() reports whether the graph contains a cycle;
  * topo_order() raises ValueError if a cycle is somehow present.

The seed tests in test_seed.py must stay green as well.
"""
from taskdag.scheduler import Scheduler


def expect_value_error(fn):
    """Assert that calling fn() raises ValueError."""
    try:
        fn()
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError("expected ValueError")


def test_self_dependency_raises_and_leaves_graph_unchanged():
    s = Scheduler()
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == []  # nothing was even registered

    s.add_task("x")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == ["x"]
    assert s.dependencies("x") == []


def test_two_task_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")  # b depends on a: legal
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "b"))  # would cycle
    # The refused edge was not recorded; the graph is unchanged.
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b"]
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("b") == ["a"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b"]


def test_transitive_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("c", "b")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "c"))  # a -> c -> b -> a
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("c") == ["b"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_new_tasks_can_still_be_attached_safely():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("a", "c")  # c is brand new, so no cycle is possible
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert s.topo_order() == ["c", "a", "b"]


def test_has_cycle_flat_cases():
    assert not Scheduler().has_cycle()
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    s.add_dependency("d", "c")
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()


def test_has_cycle_detects_injected_cycle():
    # The public API refuses to build cycles, so simulate _deps tampering.
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s._deps["a"].add("b")  # close a -> b -> a behind the API's back
    assert s.has_cycle()
    expect_value_error(s.topo_order)
    # Detecting the cycle must not have mutated the graph.
    assert s.has_cycle()


def test_has_cycle_detects_injected_self_loop():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("x")
    s._deps["x"].add("x")
    assert s.has_cycle()
    expect_value_error(s.topo_order)


def test_topo_order_still_deterministic():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("c", "a")
    s.add_dependency("d", "b")
    s.add_dependency("d", "c")
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
    assert s.topo_order() == s.topo_order()

    test_has_cycle_flat_cases()
    test_has_cycle_detects_injected_cycle()

    print("cycle tests ok")

"""A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph.

Design notes (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * The graph is kept as a single dict ``_deps`` mapping
        task name -> set(names of that task's DIRECT dependencies).
    Registering a task with no dependencies stores an empty set.
  * "task depends_on dep" means ``dep`` must run BEFORE ``task``; it is
    recorded by adding ``dep`` to ``_deps[task]``.
  * Everything is deterministic: there is no randomness, wall-clock, or
    network use anywhere, and any ordering exposed to callers is sorted.
  * ``topo_order()`` runs Kahn's algorithm with an alphabetically sorted
    frontier: whenever several tasks are simultaneously free (all of their
    dependencies already placed) it emits them in alphabetical order.

Public API (do not rename without updating callers):
  add_task(name), add_dependency(task, depends_on),
  tasks(), dependencies(name), topo_order()
"""


class Scheduler:
    def __init__(self):
        # name -> set of direct dependency names
        self._deps = {}

    # ----- graph construction --------------------------------------------
    def add_task(self, name):
        """Register a task. Idempotent: re-adding an existing task is a no-op
        and never clears its recorded dependencies."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            self._deps[name] = set()

    def add_dependency(self, task, depends_on):
        """Record that ``task`` depends on ``depends_on`` (so ``depends_on``
        must run first). Both tasks are auto-registered if new."""
        self.add_task(task)
        self.add_task(depends_on)
        self._deps[task].add(depends_on)

    # ----- graph reads ----------------------------------------------------
    def tasks(self):
        """Sorted list of all registered task names."""
        return sorted(self._deps.keys())

    def dependencies(self, name):
        """Sorted list of ``name``'s DIRECT dependencies."""
        return sorted(self._deps[name])

  add_task(name), add_dependency(task, depends_on),
  tasks(), dependencies(name), topo_order()
"""


class Scheduler:
    def __init__(self):
        # name -> set of direct dependency names
        self._deps = {}

    # ----- graph construction --------------------------------------------
    def add_task(self, name):
        """Register a task. Idempotent: re-adding an existing task is a no-op
        and never clears its recorded dependencies."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            self._deps[name] = set()

    def add_dependency(self, task, depends_on):
        """Record that ``task`` depends on ``depends_on`` (so ``depends_on``
        must run first). Both tasks are auto-registered if new."""
        self.add_task(task)
        self.add_task(depends_on)
        self._deps[task].add(depends_on)

    # ----- graph reads ----------------------------------------------------
    def tasks(self):
        """Sorted list of all registered task names."""
        return sorted(self._deps.keys())

    def dependencies(self, name):
        """Sorted list of ``name``'s DIRECT dependencies."""
        return sorted(self._deps[name])

    # ----- ordering -------------------------------------------------------
    def topo_order(self):
        """Return EVERY registered task in dependency order: each task appears
        after all of its (transitive) dependencies.

        Deterministic: Kahn's algorithm with an alphabetically sorted
        frontier. While tasks remain, the next emitted task is the
        alphabetically smallest one whose (still-unplaced) dependencies have
        all already been placed.

        Raises ValueError if the graph contains a cycle, because then no order
        can place every task after all of its dependencies.
        """
        # Work on a copy of the adjacency; the stored graph is never mutated.
        remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        order = []
        while remaining:
            # Tasks all of whose remaining dependencies are already placed;
            # sorted so the alphabetically smallest is emitted first.
            frontier = sorted(
                name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps
            )
            if not frontier:  # a cycle: every remaining task still waits
                break
            name = frontier[0]
            del remaining[name]
            order.append(name)
            # Placing ``name`` satisfies one dependency of each dependent.
            for deps in remaining.values():
                deps.discard(name)
        if remaining:
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no topological order exists for "
                "tasks %r" % (sorted(remaining),)
            )
        return order

"""Tests for cycle safety.

The scheduler must refuse to build cycles:
  * add_dependency(x, x) raises ValueError;
  * add_dependency(task, depends_on) raises ValueError -- leaving the graph
    unchanged -- when depends_on already reaches task through existing edges;
  * has_cycle() reports whether the graph contains a cycle;
  * topo_order() raises ValueError if a cycle is somehow present.

The seed tests in test_seed.py must stay green as well.
"""
from taskdag.scheduler import Scheduler


def expect_value_error(fn):
    """Assert that calling fn() raises ValueError."""
    try:
        fn()
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError("expected ValueError")


def test_self_dependency_raises_and_leaves_graph_unchanged():
    s = Scheduler()
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == []  # nothing was even registered

    s.add_task("x")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == ["x"]
    assert s.dependencies("x") == []


def test_two_task_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")  # b depends on a: legal
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "b"))  # would cycle
    # The refused edge was not recorded; the graph is unchanged.
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b"]
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("b") == ["a"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b"]


def test_transitive_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("c", "b")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "c"))  # a -> c -> b -> a
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("c") == ["b"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_new_tasks_can_still_be_attached_safely():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("a", "c")  # c is brand new, so no cycle is possible
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert s.topo_order() == ["c", "a", "b"]


def test_has_cycle_flat_cases():
    assert not Scheduler().has_cycle()
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    s.add_dependency("d", "c")
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()


def test_has_cycle_detects_injected_cycle():
    # The public API refuses to build cycles, so simulate _deps tampering.
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s._deps["a"].add("b")  # close a -> b -> a behind the API's back
    assert s.has_cycle()
    expect_value_error(s.topo_order)
    # Detecting the cycle must not have mutated the graph.
    assert s.has_cycle()


def test_has_cycle_detects_injected_self_loop():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("x")
    s._deps["x"].add("x")
    assert s.has_cycle()
    expect_value_error(s.topo_order)

    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("c", "a")
    s.add_dependency("d", "b")
    s.add_dependency("d", "c")
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
    assert s.topo_order() == s.topo_order()

# taskdag

A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph, used as a teaching
toy.

Current capabilities:
  * register tasks and dependency edges (`add_task` / `add_dependency`)
  * read the graph back (`tasks` / `dependencies`)
  * order the whole graph (`topo_order`) — Kahn's algorithm with an
    alphabetically sorted frontier, so the result is deterministic
  * ask what can run next (`ready`) — given the completed tasks, the sorted
    tasks that are not yet done and whose every direct dependency is done
  * refuse to build cycles — `add_dependency` raises `ValueError` (leaving
    the graph unchanged) for a self-dependency or an edge that would close a
    cycle; `has_cycle()` reports whether a cycle is present

See `taskdag/scheduler.py` for the design notes. Keep the adjacency design
(`name -> set of direct dependency names`); new features should build on
`_deps` rather than replacing it.

    def add_task(self, name):
        """Register a task. Idempotent: re-adding an existing task is a no-op
        and never clears its recorded dependencies."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            self._deps[name] = set()

        """Record that ``task`` depends on ``depends_on`` (so ``depends_on``
        must run first). Both tasks are auto-registered if new."""

        self.add_task(depends_on)
        self._deps[task].add(depends_on)

    def tasks(self):

        return sorted(self._deps[name])

"""Tests for cycle safety.

The scheduler must refuse to build cycles:
  * add_dependency(x, x) raises ValueError;
  * add_dependency(task, depends_on) raises ValueError -- leaving the graph
    unchanged -- when depends_on already reaches task through existing edges;
  * has_cycle() reports whether the graph contains a cycle;
  * topo_order() raises ValueError if a cycle is somehow present.

The seed tests in test_seed.py must stay green as well.
"""
from taskdag.scheduler import Scheduler


def expect_value_error(fn):
    """Assert that calling fn() raises ValueError."""
    try:
        fn()
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError("expected ValueError")


def test_self_dependency_raises_and_leaves_graph_unchanged():
    s = Scheduler()
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == []  # nothing was even registered

    s.add_task("x")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == ["x"]
    assert s.dependencies("x") == []


def test_two_task_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")  # b depends on a: legal
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "b"))  # would cycle
    # The refused edge was not recorded; the graph is unchanged.
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b"]
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("b") == ["a"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b"]


def test_transitive_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("c", "b")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "c"))  # a -> c -> b -> a
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("c") == ["b"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_new_tasks_can_still_be_attached_safely():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("a", "c")  # c is brand new, so no cycle is possible
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert s.topo_order() == ["c", "a", "b"]


def test_has_cycle_flat_cases():
    assert not Scheduler().has_cycle()
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    s.add_dependency("d", "c")
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()


def test_has_cycle_detects_injected_cycle():
    # The public API refuses to build cycles, so simulate _deps tampering.
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s._deps["a"].add("b")  # close a -> b -> a behind the API's back
    assert s.has_cycle()
    expect_value_error(s.topo_order)
    # Detecting the cycle must not have mutated the graph.
    assert s.has_cycle()


def test_has_cycle_detects_injected_self_loop():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("x")
    s._deps["x"].add("x")
    assert s.has_cycle()
    expect_value_error(s.topo_order)

    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("c", "a")
    s.add_dependency("d", "b")
    s.add_dependency("d", "c")
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
    assert s.topo_order() == s.topo_order()

# taskdag

A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph, used as a teaching
toy.

Current capabilities:
  * register tasks and dependency edges (`add_task` / `add_dependency`)
  * read the graph back (`tasks` / `dependencies`)
  * order the whole graph (`topo_order`) — Kahn's algorithm with an
    alphabetically sorted frontier, so the result is deterministic
  * ask what can run next (`ready`) — given the completed tasks, the sorted
    tasks that are not yet done and whose every direct dependency is done
  * refuse to build cycles — `add_dependency` raises `ValueError` (leaving
    the graph unchanged) for a self-dependency or an edge that would close a
    cycle; `has_cycle()` reports whether a cycle is present

See `taskdag/scheduler.py` for the design notes. Keep the adjacency design
(`name -> set of direct dependency names`); new features should build on
`_deps` rather than replacing it.

# taskdag

A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph, used as a teaching
toy.

Current capabilities:
  * register tasks and dependency edges (`add_task` / `add_dependency`)
  * read the graph back (`tasks` / `dependencies`)
  * order the whole graph (`topo_order`) — Kahn's algorithm with an
    alphabetically sorted frontier, so the result is deterministic
  * split the graph into dependency waves (`waves`) — a list of levels, each
    sorted; level 0 is the tasks with no dependencies and each later level is
    the tasks whose every direct dependency lies in an earlier level
  * ask what can run next (`ready`) — given the completed tasks, the sorted
    tasks that are not yet done and whose every direct dependency is done
  * refuse to build cycles — `add_dependency` raises `ValueError` (leaving
    the graph unchanged) for a self-dependency or an edge that would close a
    cycle; `has_cycle()` reports whether a cycle is present

See `taskdag/scheduler.py` for the design notes. Keep the adjacency design
(`name -> set of direct dependency names`); new features should build on
`_deps` rather than replacing it.

"""Tests for cycle safety.

The scheduler must refuse to build cycles:
  * add_dependency(x, x) raises ValueError;
  * add_dependency(task, depends_on) raises ValueError -- leaving the graph
    unchanged -- when depends_on already reaches task through existing edges;
  * has_cycle() reports whether the graph contains a cycle;
  * topo_order() raises ValueError if a cycle is somehow present.

"""
from taskdag.scheduler import Scheduler


def expect_value_error(fn):
    """Assert that calling fn() raises ValueError."""
    try:
        fn()
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError("expected ValueError")


def test_self_dependency_raises_and_leaves_graph_unchanged():
    s = Scheduler()
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == []  # nothing was even registered

    s.add_task("x")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == ["x"]
    assert s.dependencies("x") == []


def test_two_task_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")  # b depends on a: legal
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "b"))  # would cycle
    # The refused edge was not recorded; the graph is unchanged.
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b"]
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("b") == ["a"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b"]


def test_transitive_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("c", "b")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "c"))  # a -> c -> b -> a
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("c") == ["b"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_new_tasks_can_still_be_attached_safely():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("a", "c")  # c is brand new, so no cycle is possible
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert s.topo_order() == ["c", "a", "b"]


def test_has_cycle_flat_cases():
    assert not Scheduler().has_cycle()
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    s.add_dependency("d", "c")
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()


def test_has_cycle_detects_injected_cycle():
    # The public API refuses to build cycles, so simulate _deps tampering.
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s._deps["a"].add("b")  # close a -> b -> a behind the API's back
    assert s.has_cycle()
    expect_value_error(s.topo_order)

    assert s.has_cycle()

        when ``depends_on`` already reaches ``task`` through existing edges

        all already been placed. If a cycle remains -- every leftover task
        still waits on another -- iteration simply ends early. The stored

# taskdag

A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph, used as a teaching
toy.

Current capabilities:
  * register tasks and dependency edges (`add_task` / `add_dependency`)
  * read the graph back (`tasks` / `dependencies`)
  * order the whole graph (`topo_order`) — Kahn's algorithm with an
    alphabetically sorted frontier, so the result is deterministic
  * ask what can run next (`ready`) — given the completed tasks, the sorted
    tasks that are not yet done and whose every direct dependency is done
  * refuse to build cycles — `add_dependency` raises `ValueError` (leaving
    the graph unchanged) for a self-dependency or an edge that would close a
    cycle; `has_cycle()` reports whether a cycle is present

See `taskdag/scheduler.py` for the design notes. Keep the adjacency design
(`name -> set of direct dependency names`); new features should build on
`_deps` rather than replacing it.

# taskdag

A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph, used as a teaching
toy.

Current capabilities:
  * register tasks and dependency edges (`add_task` / `add_dependency`)
  * read the graph back (`tasks` / `dependencies`)
  * order the whole graph (`topo_order`) — Kahn's algorithm with an
    alphabetically sorted frontier, so the result is deterministic
  * split the graph into dependency waves (`waves`) — a list of levels, each
    sorted; level 0 is the tasks with no dependencies and each later level is
    the tasks whose every direct dependency lies in an earlier level
  * ask what can run next (`ready`) — given the completed tasks, the sorted
    tasks that are not yet done and whose every direct dependency is done
  * refuse to build cycles — `add_dependency` raises `ValueError` (leaving
    the graph unchanged) for a self-dependency or an edge that would close a
    cycle; `has_cycle()` reports whether a cycle is present

See `taskdag/scheduler.py` for the design notes. Keep the adjacency design
(`name -> set of direct dependency names`); new features should build on
`_deps` rather than replacing it.

class Scheduler:

        self._deps = {}

    def add_task(self, name):
        """Register a task. Idempotent: re-adding an existing task is a no-op
        and never clears its recorded dependencies."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            self._deps[name] = set()

    def _reaches(self, start, target):
        """True if ``target`` is reachable from ``start`` by following
        existing "depends on" edges (i.e. ``target`` must run before
        ``start``). Reads ``_deps`` without mutating it; safe even on a
        graph that already contains cycles."""
        seen = set()
        pending = [start]
        while pending:
            name = pending.pop()
            if name in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(name)
            if name == target:
                return True
            pending.extend(self._deps.get(name, ()))
        return False

        must run first). Both tasks are auto-registered if new.

        left exactly unchanged -- when ``task`` is ``depends_on`` itself or
        when ``depends_on`` already reaches ``task`` through existing edges
        (adding the edge would close a cycle).

        if self._reaches(depends_on, task):

                "create a cycle" % (task, depends_on, depends_on, task)
            )

        """
        done = set(done)
        return sorted(
            name
            for name, deps in self._deps.items()
            if name not in done and deps <= done
        )

    # ----- ordering -------------------------------------------------------
    def _kahn(self):
        """Deterministic Kahn's algorithm over a copy of the graph.

        Yields task names as they are placed: the next emitted task is the
        alphabetically smallest one whose (still-unplaced) dependencies have
        all already been placed. If a cycle remains -- every leftover task
        still waits on another -- iteration simply ends early. The stored
        graph is never mutated.
        """
        # Work on a copy of the adjacency; the stored graph is never mutated.
        remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        while remaining:
            # Tasks all of whose remaining dependencies are already placed;
            # sorted so the alphabetically smallest is emitted first.
            frontier = sorted(
                name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps
            )
            if not frontier:  # a cycle: every remaining task still waits
                return
            name = frontier[0]
            del remaining[name]
            yield name
            # Placing ``name`` satisfies one dependency of each dependent.
            for deps in remaining.values():
                deps.discard(name)

    def topo_order(self):
        """Return EVERY registered task in dependency order: each task appears
        after all of its (transitive) dependencies.

        Deterministic: see ``_kahn``. ``add_dependency`` keeps the graph free
        of cycles by construction, but if a cycle is somehow present (e.g.
        ``_deps`` was modified directly) no order can place every task after
        all of its dependencies, and ValueError is raised.
        """
        order = list(self._kahn())
        if len(order) != len(self._deps):
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no topological order exists for "
                "tasks %r" % (sorted(set(self._deps) - set(order)),)
            )
        return order

    def has_cycle(self):
        """True if the current graph contains any cycle (a self-loop or a
        closed loop of dependency edges), which makes ordering impossible."""
        return sum(1 for _ in self._kahn()) != len(self._deps)

    # ----- waves (layering) ------------------------------------------------
    def waves(self):
        """Decompose the graph into dependency waves: a list of levels, each
        level a SORTED list of task names.

        Level 0 is exactly the tasks that have no dependencies. For k > 0,
        level k is exactly the tasks all of whose DIRECT dependencies appear
        in earlier levels (< k): a task with no dependencies sits at level 0,
        and otherwise a task sits one level past its latest direct dependency,
        i.e. at the length of the longest dependency chain ending at it. Every
        registered task therefore appears in exactly one level, and no task in
        a level depends on another task of the same level.

        Deterministic: levels are produced in order and each is sorted
        alphabetically. Raises ValueError if a cycle is present (possible only
        if ``_deps`` was modified directly), because then some task can never
        have all of its dependencies placed in earlier levels.
        """
        # Work on a copy of the adjacency; the stored graph is never mutated.
        remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        levels = []
        while remaining:
            # Next level: tasks whose remaining dependencies all lie in
            # already-emitted (earlier) levels; sorted alphabetically.
            level = sorted(
                name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps
            )
            if not level:  # a cycle: every remaining task still waits
                break
            levels.append(level)
            for name in level:
                del remaining[name]
            # No two members of one level depend on each other (each member's
            # deps are all in earlier levels), so removing the whole level at
            # once is safe.
            for deps in remaining.values():
                deps.difference_update(level)
        if remaining:
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no wave decomposition exists for "
                "tasks %r" % (sorted(remaining),)
            )
        return levels

# taskdag

A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph, used as a teaching
toy.

Current capabilities:
  * register tasks and dependency edges (`add_task` / `add_dependency`)
  * remove a task and every edge that references it (`remove_task`) — raises
    `KeyError` if the task is not registered
  * read the graph back (`tasks` / `dependencies`)
  * order the whole graph (`topo_order`) — Kahn's algorithm with an
    alphabetically sorted frontier, so the result is deterministic
  * split the graph into dependency waves (`waves`) — a list of levels, each
    sorted; level 0 is the tasks with no dependencies and each later level is
    the tasks whose every direct dependency lies in an earlier level
  * ask what can run next (`ready`) — given the completed tasks, the sorted
    tasks that are not yet done and whose every direct dependency is done
  * refuse to build cycles — `add_dependency` raises `ValueError` (leaving
    the graph unchanged) for a self-dependency or an edge that would close a
    cycle; `has_cycle()` reports whether a cycle is present

See `taskdag/scheduler.py` for the design notes. Keep the adjacency design
(`name -> set of direct dependency names`); new features should build on
`_deps` rather than replacing it.

The scheduler must refuse to build cycles:
  * add_dependency(x, x) raises ValueError;
  * add_dependency(task, depends_on) raises ValueError -- leaving the graph
    unchanged -- when depends_on already reaches task through existing edges;
  * has_cycle() reports whether the graph contains a cycle;
  * topo_order() raises ValueError if a cycle is somehow present.

from taskdag.scheduler import Scheduler


def expect_value_error(fn):
    """Assert that calling fn() raises ValueError."""
    try:
        fn()
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError("expected ValueError")


def test_self_dependency_raises_and_leaves_graph_unchanged():
    s = Scheduler()
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == []  # nothing was even registered

    s.add_task("x")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == ["x"]
    assert s.dependencies("x") == []


def test_two_task_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")  # b depends on a: legal
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "b"))  # would cycle
    # The refused edge was not recorded; the graph is unchanged.
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b"]
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("b") == ["a"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b"]


def test_transitive_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("c", "b")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "c"))  # a -> c -> b -> a
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("c") == ["b"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_new_tasks_can_still_be_attached_safely():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("a", "c")  # c is brand new, so no cycle is possible
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert s.topo_order() == ["c", "a", "b"]

    assert not Scheduler().has_cycle()
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    s.add_dependency("d", "c")
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()

"""A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph.

Design notes (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * The graph is kept as a single dict ``_deps`` mapping
        task name -> set(names of that task's DIRECT dependencies).
    Registering a task with no dependencies stores an empty set.
  * "task depends_on dep" means ``dep`` must run BEFORE ``task``; it is
    recorded by adding ``dep`` to ``_deps[task]``.
  * Everything is deterministic: there is no randomness, wall-clock, or
    network use anywhere, and any ordering exposed to callers is sorted.
  * ``topo_order()`` runs Kahn's algorithm with an alphabetically sorted
    frontier: whenever several tasks are simultaneously free (all of their
    dependencies already placed) it emits them in alphabetical order.
  * The graph is kept acyclic by construction: ``add_dependency`` refuses
    self-dependencies and edges that would close a cycle (raising ValueError
    and leaving the graph unchanged). ``has_cycle()`` reports whether a cycle
    is present anyway (possible only if ``_deps`` is tampered with).
  * ``ready(done)`` answers "what can start next": given the set of tasks
    already completed, the tasks that are not done and whose every DIRECT
    dependency is done.
  * ``remove_task(name)`` deletes a task and every edge that references it:
    the task's own dependency entry vanishes with it, and the name is dropped
    from every other task's dependency set. It raises KeyError if ``name`` is
    not registered.
  * ``waves()`` splits the graph into levels: level 0 is exactly the tasks
    with no dependencies, and each later level holds the tasks whose every
    DIRECT dependency appears in an earlier level, so every registered task
    lands in exactly one level.
  * ``run(runner)`` executes the whole graph: ``runner(name)`` is called
    exactly once per task, in ``topo_order()`` order, and the returned dict
    maps every task name to ``'ok'``. Failures are not handled yet: every
    ``runner`` call is assumed to succeed.

Public API (do not rename without updating callers):
  add_task(name), add_dependency(task, depends_on), remove_task(name),
  tasks(), dependencies(name), ready(done), waves(), has_cycle(),
  topo_order(), run(runner)
"""


class Scheduler:
    def __init__(self):
        # name -> set of direct dependency names
        self._deps = {}

    # ----- graph construction --------------------------------------------
    def add_task(self, name):
        """Register a task. Idempotent: re-adding an existing task is a no-op
        and never clears its recorded dependencies."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            self._deps[name] = set()

    def _reaches(self, start, target):
        """True if ``target`` is reachable from ``start`` by following
        existing "depends on" edges (i.e. ``target`` must run before
        ``start``). Reads ``_deps`` without mutating it; safe even on a
        graph that already contains cycles."""
        seen = set()
        pending = [start]
        while pending:
            name = pending.pop()
            if name in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(name)
            if name == target:
                return True
            pending.extend(self._deps.get(name, ()))
        return False

    def add_dependency(self, task, depends_on):
        """Record that ``task`` depends on ``depends_on`` (so ``depends_on``
        must run first). Both tasks are auto-registered if new.

        Cycle safety: the edge is refused with ValueError -- and the graph is
        left exactly unchanged -- when ``task`` is ``depends_on`` itself or
        when ``depends_on`` already reaches ``task`` through existing edges
        (adding the edge would close a cycle).
        """
        if task == depends_on:
            raise ValueError("a task cannot depend on itself: %r" % (task,))
        if self._reaches(depends_on, task):
            raise ValueError(
                "refusing to record that %r depends on %r: %r already "
                "depends on %r through existing edges, so this edge would "
                "create a cycle" % (task, depends_on, depends_on, task)
            )
        self.add_task(task)
        self.add_task(depends_on)
        self._deps[task].add(depends_on)

    def remove_task(self, name):
        """Remove ``name`` from the graph together with every edge that
        references it: its own dependency entries are deleted with it, and
        ``name`` is dropped from every other task's dependency set (so no
        other task keeps waiting on a task that no longer exists).

        Raises KeyError if ``name`` is not a registered task. Removing a task
        cannot introduce a cycle: the graph stays acyclic if it was acyclic.
        """
        if name not in self._deps:
            raise KeyError(name)
        del self._deps[name]
        for deps in self._deps.values():
            deps.discard(name)

    # ----- graph reads ----------------------------------------------------
    def tasks(self):
        """Sorted list of all registered task names."""
        return sorted(self._deps.keys())

    def dependencies(self, name):
        """Sorted list of ``name``'s DIRECT dependencies."""
        return sorted(self._deps[name])

    # ----- readiness ------------------------------------------------------
    def ready(self, done):
        """Sorted list of registered tasks that can start next: tasks that
        are NOT in ``done`` and whose every DIRECT dependency IS in ``done``.

        ``done`` may be any iterable of task names; order and duplicates in
        it do not matter, and names it holds that are not registered are
        simply ignored.
        """
        done = set(done)
        return sorted(
            name
            for name, deps in self._deps.items()
            if name not in done and deps <= done
        )

    # ----- ordering -------------------------------------------------------
    def _kahn(self):
        """Deterministic Kahn's algorithm over a copy of the graph.

        Yields task names as they are placed: the next emitted task is the
        alphabetically smallest one whose (still-unplaced) dependencies have
        all already been placed. If a cycle remains -- every leftover task
        still waits on another -- iteration simply ends early. The stored
        graph is never mutated.
        """
        # Work on a copy of the adjacency; the stored graph is never mutated.
        remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        while remaining:
            # Tasks all of whose remaining dependencies are already placed;
            # sorted so the alphabetically smallest is emitted first.
            frontier = sorted(
                name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps
            )
            if not frontier:  # a cycle: every remaining task still waits
                return
            name = frontier[0]
            del remaining[name]
            yield name
            # Placing ``name`` satisfies one dependency of each dependent.
            for deps in remaining.values():
                deps.discard(name)

    def topo_order(self):
        """Return EVERY registered task in dependency order: each task appears
        after all of its (transitive) dependencies.

        Deterministic: see ``_kahn``. ``add_dependency`` keeps the graph free
        of cycles by construction, but if a cycle is somehow present (e.g.
        ``_deps`` was modified directly) no order can place every task after
        all of its dependencies, and ValueError is raised.
        """
        order = list(self._kahn())
        if len(order) != len(self._deps):
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no topological order exists for "
                "tasks %r" % (sorted(set(self._deps) - set(order)),)
            )
        return order

    def has_cycle(self):
        """True if the current graph contains any cycle (a self-loop or a
        closed loop of dependency edges), which makes ordering impossible."""
        return sum(1 for _ in self._kahn()) != len(self._deps)

    # ----- waves (layering) ------------------------------------------------
    def waves(self):
        """Decompose the graph into dependency waves: a list of levels, each
        level a SORTED list of task names.

        Level 0 is exactly the tasks that have no dependencies. For k > 0,
        level k is exactly the tasks all of whose DIRECT dependencies appear
        in earlier levels (< k): a task with no dependencies sits at level 0,
        and otherwise a task sits one level past its latest direct dependency,
        i.e. at the length of the longest dependency chain ending at it. Every
        registered task therefore appears in exactly one level, and no task in
        a level depends on another task of the same level.

        Deterministic: levels are produced in order and each is sorted
        alphabetically. Raises ValueError if a cycle is present (possible only
        if ``_deps`` was modified directly), because then some task can never
        have all of its dependencies placed in earlier levels.
        """
        # Work on a copy of the adjacency; the stored graph is never mutated.
        remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        levels = []
        while remaining:
            # Next level: tasks whose remaining dependencies all lie in
            # already-emitted (earlier) levels; sorted alphabetically.
            level = sorted(
                name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps
            )
            if not level:  # a cycle: every remaining task still waits
                break
            levels.append(level)
            for name in level:
                del remaining[name]
            # No two members of one level depend on each other (each member's
            # deps are all in earlier levels), so removing the whole level at
            # once is safe.
            for deps in remaining.values():
                deps.difference_update(level)
        if remaining:
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no wave decomposition exists for "
                "tasks %r" % (sorted(remaining),)
            )
        return levels

    # ----- execution -------------------------------------------------------
    def run(self, runner):
        """Execute the graph: call ``runner(name)`` exactly once per task, in
        ``topo_order()`` order, so each task runs only after every one of its
        (transitive) dependencies has already run.

        Returns a status dict mapping every task name to the string ``'ok'``.
        Failures are not handled yet -- every ``runner`` call is assumed to
        succeed, and anything it raises simply propagates. A cycle (possible
        only if ``_deps`` was modified directly) raises ValueError, via
        ``topo_order()``, before any task has run. Pure execution: ``_deps``
        is never mutated.
        """
        status = {}
        for name in self.topo_order():
            runner(name)
            status[name] = "ok"
        return status

# taskdag

A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph, used as a teaching
toy.

Current capabilities:
  * register tasks and dependency edges (`add_task` / `add_dependency`)
  * remove a task and every edge that references it (`remove_task`) — raises
    `KeyError` if the task is not registered
  * read the graph back (`tasks` / `dependencies`)
  * order the whole graph (`topo_order`) — Kahn's algorithm with an
    alphabetically sorted frontier, so the result is deterministic
  * run the whole graph (`run`) — calls a runner once per task in
    `topo_order` order and reports every task as `'ok'`
  * split the graph into dependency waves (`waves`) — a list of levels, each
    sorted; level 0 is the tasks with no dependencies and each later level is
    the tasks whose every direct dependency lies in an earlier level
  * ask what can run next (`ready`) — given the completed tasks, the sorted
    tasks that are not yet done and whose every direct dependency is done
  * refuse to build cycles — `add_dependency` raises `ValueError` (leaving
    the graph unchanged) for a self-dependency or an edge that would close a
    cycle; `has_cycle()` reports whether a cycle is present

See `taskdag/scheduler.py` for the design notes. Keep the adjacency design
(`name -> set of direct dependency names`); new features should build on
`_deps` rather than replacing it.

"""Tests for cycle safety.

The scheduler must refuse to build cycles:
  * add_dependency(x, x) raises ValueError;
  * add_dependency(task, depends_on) raises ValueError -- leaving the graph
    unchanged -- when depends_on already reaches task through existing edges;
  * has_cycle() reports whether the graph contains a cycle;
  * topo_order() raises ValueError if a cycle is somehow present.

The seed tests in test_seed.py must stay green as well.
"""
from taskdag.scheduler import Scheduler


def expect_value_error(fn):
    """Assert that calling fn() raises ValueError."""
    try:
        fn()
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError("expected ValueError")


def test_self_dependency_raises_and_leaves_graph_unchanged():
    s = Scheduler()
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == []  # nothing was even registered

    s.add_task("x")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("x", "x"))
    assert s.tasks() == ["x"]
    assert s.dependencies("x") == []


def test_two_task_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")  # b depends on a: legal
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "b"))  # would cycle
    # The refused edge was not recorded; the graph is unchanged.
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b"]
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("b") == ["a"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b"]


def test_transitive_cycle_refused():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("c", "b")
    expect_value_error(lambda: s.add_dependency("a", "c"))  # a -> c -> b -> a
    assert s.dependencies("a") == []
    assert s.dependencies("c") == ["b"]
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_new_tasks_can_still_be_attached_safely():
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("a", "c")  # c is brand new, so no cycle is possible
    assert s.tasks() == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert s.topo_order() == ["c", "a", "b"]


def test_has_cycle_flat_cases():
    assert not Scheduler().has_cycle()
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()
    s.add_dependency("d", "c")
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    assert not s.has_cycle()


def test_has_cycle_detects_injected_cycle():
    # The public API refuses to build cycles, so simulate _deps tampering.
    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s._deps["a"].add("b")  # close a -> b -> a behind the API's back
    assert s.has_cycle()

    s = Scheduler()
    s.add_task("x")
    s._deps["x"].add("x")
    assert s.has_cycle()
    expect_value_error(s.topo_order)


def test_topo_order_still_deterministic():

    s.add_dependency("b", "a")
    s.add_dependency("c", "a")
    s.add_dependency("d", "b")
    s.add_dependency("d", "c")
    assert s.topo_order() == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
    assert s.topo_order() == s.topo_order()

"""A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph.

Design notes (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * The graph is kept as a single dict ``_deps`` mapping
        task name -> set(names of that task's DIRECT dependencies).
    Registering a task with no dependencies stores an empty set.
  * "task depends_on dep" means ``dep`` must run BEFORE ``task``; it is
    recorded by adding ``dep`` to ``_deps[task]``.
  * Everything is deterministic: there is no randomness, wall-clock, or
    network use anywhere, and any ordering exposed to callers is sorted.
  * ``topo_order()`` runs Kahn's algorithm with an alphabetically sorted
    frontier: whenever several tasks are simultaneously free (all of their
    dependencies already placed) it emits them in alphabetical order.
  * The graph is kept acyclic by construction: ``add_dependency`` refuses
    self-dependencies and edges that would close a cycle (raising ValueError
    and leaving the graph unchanged). ``has_cycle()`` reports whether a cycle
    is present anyway (possible only if ``_deps`` is tampered with).
  * ``ready(done)`` answers "what can start next": given the set of tasks
    already completed, the tasks that are not done and whose every DIRECT
    dependency is done.
  * ``remove_task(name)`` deletes a task and every edge that references it:
    the task's own dependency entry vanishes with it, and the name is dropped
    from every other task's dependency set. It raises KeyError if ``name`` is
    not registered.
  * ``waves()`` splits the graph into levels: level 0 is exactly the tasks
    with no dependencies, and each later level holds the tasks whose every
    DIRECT dependency appears in an earlier level, so every registered task
    lands in exactly one level.
  * ``run(runner)`` executes the whole graph: ``runner(name)`` is called
    exactly once per task, in ``topo_order()`` order, and the returned dict
    maps every task name to ``'ok'``. Failures are not handled yet: every
    ``runner`` call is assumed to succeed.

Public API (do not rename without updating callers):
  add_task(name), add_dependency(task, depends_on), remove_task(name),
  tasks(), dependencies(name), ready(done), waves(), has_cycle(),
  topo_order(), run(runner)
"""


class Scheduler:
    def __init__(self):
        # name -> set of direct dependency names
        self._deps = {}

    # ----- graph construction --------------------------------------------
    def add_task(self, name):
        """Register a task. Idempotent: re-adding an existing task is a no-op
        and never clears its recorded dependencies."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            self._deps[name] = set()

    def _reaches(self, start, target):
        """True if ``target`` is reachable from ``start`` by following
        existing "depends on" edges (i.e. ``target`` must run before
        ``start``). Reads ``_deps`` without mutating it; safe even on a
        graph that already contains cycles."""
        seen = set()
        pending = [start]
        while pending:
            name = pending.pop()
            if name in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(name)
            if name == target:
                return True
            pending.extend(self._deps.get(name, ()))
        return False

    def add_dependency(self, task, depends_on):
        """Record that ``task`` depends on ``depends_on`` (so ``depends_on``
        must run first). Both tasks are auto-registered if new.

        Cycle safety: the edge is refused with ValueError -- and the graph is
        left exactly unchanged -- when ``task`` is ``depends_on`` itself or
        when ``depends_on`` already reaches ``task`` through existing edges
        (adding the edge would close a cycle).
        """
        if task == depends_on:
            raise ValueError("a task cannot depend on itself: %r" % (task,))
        if self._reaches(depends_on, task):
            raise ValueError(
                "refusing to record that %r depends on %r: %r already "
                "depends on %r through existing edges, so this edge would "
                "create a cycle" % (task, depends_on, depends_on, task)
            )
        self.add_task(task)
        self.add_task(depends_on)
        self._deps[task].add(depends_on)

    def remove_task(self, name):
        """Remove ``name`` from the graph together with every edge that
        references it: its own dependency entries are deleted with it, and
        ``name`` is dropped from every other task's dependency set (so no
        other task keeps waiting on a task that no longer exists).

        Raises KeyError if ``name`` is not a registered task. Removing a task
        cannot introduce a cycle: the graph stays acyclic if it was acyclic.
        """
        if name not in self._deps:
            raise KeyError(name)
        del self._deps[name]
        for deps in self._deps.values():
            deps.discard(name)

    # ----- graph reads ----------------------------------------------------
    def tasks(self):
        """Sorted list of all registered task names."""
        return sorted(self._deps.keys())

    def dependencies(self, name):
        """Sorted list of ``name``'s DIRECT dependencies."""
        return sorted(self._deps[name])

    # ----- readiness ------------------------------------------------------
    def ready(self, done):
        """Sorted list of registered tasks that can start next: tasks that
        are NOT in ``done`` and whose every DIRECT dependency IS in ``done``.

        ``done`` may be any iterable of task names; order and duplicates in
        it do not matter, and names it holds that are not registered are
        simply ignored.
        """
        done = set(done)
        return sorted(
            name
            for name, deps in self._deps.items()
            if name not in done and deps <= done
        )

    # ----- ordering -------------------------------------------------------
    def _kahn(self):
        """Deterministic Kahn's algorithm over a copy of the graph.

        Yields task names as they are placed: the next emitted task is the
        alphabetically smallest one whose (still-unplaced) dependencies have
        all already been placed. If a cycle remains -- every leftover task
        still waits on another -- iteration simply ends early. The stored
        graph is never mutated.
        """
        # Work on a copy of the adjacency; the stored graph is never mutated.
        remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        while remaining:
            # Tasks all of whose remaining dependencies are already placed;
            # sorted so the alphabetically smallest is emitted first.
            frontier = sorted(
                name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps
            )
            if not frontier:  # a cycle: every remaining task still waits
                return
            name = frontier[0]
            del remaining[name]
            yield name
            # Placing ``name`` satisfies one dependency of each dependent.
            for deps in remaining.values():
                deps.discard(name)

    def topo_order(self):
        """Return EVERY registered task in dependency order: each task appears
        after all of its (transitive) dependencies.

        Deterministic: see ``_kahn``. ``add_dependency`` keeps the graph free
        of cycles by construction, but if a cycle is somehow present (e.g.
        ``_deps`` was modified directly) no order can place every task after
        all of its dependencies, and ValueError is raised.
        """
        order = list(self._kahn())
        if len(order) != len(self._deps):
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no topological order exists for "
                "tasks %r" % (sorted(set(self._deps) - set(order)),)
            )
        return order

    def has_cycle(self):
        """True if the current graph contains any cycle (a self-loop or a
        closed loop of dependency edges), which makes ordering impossible."""
        return sum(1 for _ in self._kahn()) != len(self._deps)

    # ----- waves (layering) ------------------------------------------------
    def waves(self):
        """Decompose the graph into dependency waves: a list of levels, each
        level a SORTED list of task names.

        Level 0 is exactly the tasks that have no dependencies. For k > 0,
        level k is exactly the tasks all of whose DIRECT dependencies appear
        in earlier levels (< k): a task with no dependencies sits at level 0,
        and otherwise a task sits one level past its latest direct dependency,
        i.e. at the length of the longest dependency chain ending at it. Every
        registered task therefore appears in exactly one level, and no task in
        a level depends on another task of the same level.

        Deterministic: levels are produced in order and each is sorted
        alphabetically. Raises ValueError if a cycle is present (possible only
        if ``_deps`` was modified directly), because then some task can never
        have all of its dependencies placed in earlier levels.
        """
        # Work on a copy of the adjacency; the stored graph is never mutated.
        remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        levels = []
        while remaining:
            # Next level: tasks whose remaining dependencies all lie in
            # already-emitted (earlier) levels; sorted alphabetically.
            level = sorted(
                name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps
            )
            if not level:  # a cycle: every remaining task still waits
                break
            levels.append(level)
            for name in level:
                del remaining[name]
            # No two members of one level depend on each other (each member's
            # deps are all in earlier levels), so removing the whole level at
            # once is safe.
            for deps in remaining.values():
                deps.difference_update(level)
        if remaining:
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no wave decomposition exists for "
                "tasks %r" % (sorted(remaining),)
            )
        return levels

    # ----- execution -------------------------------------------------------
    def run(self, runner):
        """Execute the graph: call ``runner(name)`` exactly once per task, in
        ``topo_order()`` order, so each task runs only after every one of its
        (transitive) dependencies has already run.

        Returns a status dict mapping every task name to the string ``'ok'``.
        Failures are not handled yet -- every ``runner`` call is assumed to
        succeed, and anything it raises simply propagates. A cycle (possible
        only if ``_deps`` was modified directly) raises ValueError, via
        ``topo_order()``, before any task has run. Pure execution: ``_deps``
        is never mutated.
        """
        status = {}
        for name in self.topo_order():
            runner(name)
            status[name] = "ok"
        return status

# taskdag

A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph, used as a teaching
toy.

Current capabilities:
  * register tasks and dependency edges (`add_task` / `add_dependency`)
  * remove a task and every edge that references it (`remove_task`) — raises
    `KeyError` if the task is not registered
  * read the graph back (`tasks` / `dependencies`)
  * order the whole graph (`topo_order`) — Kahn's algorithm with an
    alphabetically sorted frontier, so the result is deterministic
  * run the whole graph (`run`) — calls a runner once per task in
    `topo_order` order and reports every task as `'ok'`
  * split the graph into dependency waves (`waves`) — a list of levels, each
    sorted; level 0 is the tasks with no dependencies and each later level is
    the tasks whose every direct dependency lies in an earlier level
  * ask what can run next (`ready`) — given the completed tasks, the sorted
    tasks that are not yet done and whose every direct dependency is done
  * refuse to build cycles — `add_dependency` raises `ValueError` (leaving
    the graph unchanged) for a self-dependency or an edge that would close a
    cycle; `has_cycle()` reports whether a cycle is present

See `taskdag/scheduler.py` for the design notes. Keep the adjacency design
(`name -> set of direct dependency names`); new features should build on
`_deps` rather than replacing it.

    try:

    raise AssertionError("expected ValueError")


def test_self_dependency_raises_and_leaves_graph_unchanged():
    s = Scheduler()

    assert s.dependencies("a") == []

"""A tiny deterministic task scheduler over a dependency graph.

Design notes (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * The graph is kept as a single dict ``_deps`` mapping
        task name -> set(names of that task's DIRECT dependencies).
    Registering a task with no dependencies stores an empty set.
  * "task depends_on dep" means ``dep`` must run BEFORE ``task``; it is
    recorded by adding ``dep`` to ``_deps[task]``.
  * Everything is deterministic: there is no randomness, wall-clock, or
    network use anywhere, and any ordering exposed to callers is sorted.
  * ``topo_order()`` runs Kahn's algorithm with an alphabetically sorted
    frontier: whenever several tasks are simultaneously free (all of their
    dependencies already placed) it emits them in alphabetical order.
  * The graph is kept acyclic by construction: ``add_dependency`` refuses
    self-dependencies and edges that would close a cycle (raising ValueError
    and leaving the graph unchanged). ``has_cycle()`` reports whether a cycle
    is present anyway (possible only if ``_deps`` is tampered with).
  * ``ready(done)`` answers "what can start next": given the set of tasks
    already completed, the tasks that are not done and whose every DIRECT
    dependency is done.
  * ``remove_task(name)`` deletes a task and every edge that references it:
    the task's own dependency entry vanishes with it, and the name is dropped
    from every other task's dependency set. It raises KeyError if ``name`` is
    not registered.
  * ``waves()`` splits the graph into levels: level 0 is exactly the tasks
    with no dependencies, and each later level holds the tasks whose every
    DIRECT dependency appears in an earlier level, so every registered task
    lands in exactly one level.
  * ``run(runner)`` executes the whole graph: ``runner(name)`` is called
    exactly once per task, in ``topo_order()`` order, and the returned dict
    maps every task name to ``'ok'``. Failures are not handled yet: every
    ``runner`` call is assumed to succeed.

Public API (do not rename without updating callers):
  add_task(name), add_dependency(task, depends_on), remove_task(name),
  tasks(), dependencies(name), ready(done), waves(), has_cycle(),
  topo_order(), run(runner)
"""


class Scheduler:
    def __init__(self):
        # name -> set of direct dependency names
        self._deps = {}

    # ----- graph construction --------------------------------------------
    def add_task(self, name):
        """Register a task. Idempotent: re-adding an existing task is a no-op
        and never clears its recorded dependencies."""
        if name not in self._deps:
            self._deps[name] = set()

    def _reaches(self, start, target):
        """True if ``target`` is reachable from ``start`` by following
        existing "depends on" edges (i.e. ``target`` must run before
        ``start``). Reads ``_deps`` without mutating it; safe even on a
        graph that already contains cycles."""
        seen = set()
        pending = [start]
        while pending:
            name = pending.pop()
            if name in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(name)
            if name == target:
                return True
            pending.extend(self._deps.get(name, ()))
        return False

    def add_dependency(self, task, depends_on):
        """Record that ``task`` depends on ``depends_on`` (so ``depends_on``
        must run first). Both tasks are auto-registered if new.

        Cycle safety: the edge is refused with ValueError -- and the graph is
        left exactly unchanged -- when ``task`` is ``depends_on`` itself or
        when ``depends_on`` already reaches ``task`` through existing edges
        (adding the edge would close a cycle).
        """
        if task == depends_on:
            raise ValueError("a task cannot depend on itself: %r" % (task,))
        if self._reaches(depends_on, task):
            raise ValueError(
                "refusing to record that %r depends on %r: %r already "
                "depends on %r through existing edges, so this edge would "
                "create a cycle" % (task, depends_on, depends_on, task)
            )
        self.add_task(task)
        self.add_task(depends_on)
        self._deps[task].add(depends_on)

    def remove_task(self, name):
        """Remove ``name`` from the graph together with every edge that
        references it: its own dependency entries are deleted with it, and
        ``name`` is dropped from every other task's dependency set (so no
        other task keeps waiting on a task that no longer exists).

        Raises KeyError if ``name`` is not a registered task. Removing a task
        cannot introduce a cycle: the graph stays acyclic if it was acyclic.
        """
        if name not in self._deps:
            raise KeyError(name)
        del self._deps[name]
        for deps in self._deps.values():
            deps.discard(name)

    # ----- graph reads ----------------------------------------------------
    def tasks(self):
        """Sorted list of all registered task names."""
        return sorted(self._deps.keys())

    def dependencies(self, name):
        """Sorted list of ``name``'s DIRECT dependencies."""
        return sorted(self._deps[name])

    # ----- readiness ------------------------------------------------------
    def ready(self, done):
        """Sorted list of registered tasks that can start next: tasks that
        are NOT in ``done`` and whose every DIRECT dependency IS in ``done``.

        ``done`` may be any iterable of task names; order and duplicates in
        it do not matter, and names it holds that are not registered are
        simply ignored.
        """
        done = set(done)
        return sorted(
            name
            for name, deps in self._deps.items()
            if name not in done and deps <= done
        )

    # ----- ordering -------------------------------------------------------
    def _kahn(self):
        """Deterministic Kahn's algorithm over a copy of the graph.

        Yields task names as they are placed: the next emitted task is the
        alphabetically smallest one whose (still-unplaced) dependencies have
        all already been placed. If a cycle remains -- every leftover task
        still waits on another -- iteration simply ends early. The stored
        graph is never mutated.
        """
        # Work on a copy of the adjacency; the stored graph is never mutated.
        remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        while remaining:
            # Tasks all of whose remaining dependencies are already placed;
            # sorted so the alphabetically smallest is emitted first.
            frontier = sorted(
                name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps
            )
            if not frontier:  # a cycle: every remaining task still waits
                return
            name = frontier[0]
            del remaining[name]
            yield name
            # Placing ``name`` satisfies one dependency of each dependent.
            for deps in remaining.values():
                deps.discard(name)

    def topo_order(self):
        """Return EVERY registered task in dependency order: each task appears
        after all of its (transitive) dependencies.

        Deterministic: see ``_kahn``. ``add_dependency`` keeps the graph free
        of cycles by construction, but if a cycle is somehow present (e.g.
        ``_deps`` was modified directly) no order can place every task after
        all of its dependencies, and ValueError is raised.
        """
        order = list(self._kahn())
        if len(order) != len(self._deps):
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no topological order exists for "
                "tasks %r" % (sorted(set(self._deps) - set(order)),)
            )
        return order

    def has_cycle(self):
        """True if the current graph contains any cycle (a self-loop or a
        closed loop of dependency edges), which makes ordering impossible."""
        return sum(1 for _ in self._kahn()) != len(self._deps)

    # ----- waves (layering) ------------------------------------------------
    def waves(self):
        """Decompose the graph into dependency waves: a list of levels, each
        level a SORTED list of task names.

        Level 0 is exactly the tasks that have no dependencies. For k > 0,
        level k is exactly the tasks all of whose DIRECT dependencies appear
        in earlier levels (< k): a task with no dependencies sits at level 0,
        and otherwise a task sits one level past its latest direct dependency,
        i.e. at the length of the longest dependency chain ending at it. Every
        registered task therefore appears in exactly one level, and no task in
        a level depends on another task of the same level.

        Deterministic: levels are produced in order and each is sorted
        alphabetically. Raises ValueError if a cycle is present (possible only
        if ``_deps`` was modified directly), because then some task can never
        have all of its dependencies placed in earlier levels.
        """
        # Work on a copy of the adjacency; the stored graph is never mutated.
        remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in self._deps.items()}
        levels = []
        while remaining:
            # Next level: tasks whose remaining dependencies all lie in
            # already-emitted (earlier) levels; sorted alphabetically.
            level = sorted(
                name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps
            )
            if not level:  # a cycle: every remaining task still waits
                break
            levels.append(level)
            for name in level:
                del remaining[name]
            # No two members of one level depend on each other (each member's
            # deps are all in earlier levels), so removing the whole level at
            # once is safe.
            for deps in remaining.values():
                deps.difference_update(level)
        if remaining:
            raise ValueError(
                "dependency cycle detected; no wave decomposition exists for "
                "tasks %r" % (sorted(remaining),)
            )
        return levels

    # ----- execution -------------------------------------------------------
    def run(self, runner):
        """Execute the graph: call ``runner(name)`` exactly once per task, in
        ``topo_order()`` order, so each task runs only after every one of its
        (transitive) dependencies has already run.

        Returns a status dict mapping every task name to the string ``'ok'``.
        Failures are not handled yet -- every ``runner`` call is assumed to
        succeed, and anything it raises simply propagates. A cycle (possible
        only if ``_deps`` was modified directly) raises ValueError, via
        ``topo_order()``, before any task has run. Pure execution: ``_deps``
        is never mutated.
        """
        status = {}
        for name in self.topo_order():
            runner(name)
            status[name] = "ok"
        return status
